clue.text: Force most of the decay

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut off
rust is the decay of iron

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently being told to push the bulk of the rot along.
explanation.walkthrough: THRUST is TH plus RUST; 'Force' reads as a verb in the surface but the definition works as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is a driving push, and force in physics or everyday speech can name that same propulsive power.

clue.text: Master the care problem

indicators.note: a problem is something gone wrong, so these letters have been thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to get on top of a difficulty with looking after someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a verb meaning overcome, but it is the noun for a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male classroom instructor, so master is an old-fashioned synonym for a school teacher.

clue.text: Animal starts to rub himself in nut oil

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only the initials are kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A creature begins smearing itself with oil pressed from nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to picture an animal oiling itself; really only the opening letters of the last five words matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros, shortened to rhino, is a large horned mammal of Africa and Asia, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Served up aspic in a tasting sample — that's nasty!

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from the whole, so a run of letters is lifted out
in a down clue something served up goes upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of aspic, in, a and the start of tasting

explanation.surface: A diner tries a forkful of the savoury jelly and pulls a face.
explanation.walkthrough: The run C-I-N-A-T-A-S sits inside the phrase and is read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish or wicked, so it is a strong, colourful synonym for something thoroughly unpleasant or vile.

clue.text: Cut wood conceals nothing

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a grove is a small wood
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Felled timber turns out to be hiding nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut wood' reads as one phrase about timber, but 'Cut' alone is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel cut into a surface, so a cut is a fair noun synonym.

clue.text: Lifted title regularly to gain mark of honour

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: rose is the past tense of rise, meaning went up
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone raised in rank wins a title and with it some honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' is intransitive here: rose, as in went up, not raised something.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded to prizewinners at shows, so it is a token marking an achievement or distinction.

clue.text: Lacking fragrance, love? Manufacture or use LSD

indicators.note: to manufacture is to make something new from raw material, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist wonders whether to make or take a drug with no smell.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD is a hallucinogenic drug, which suits the surface; here it just supplies three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odourless gives off no smell at all, so it has no scent or perfume of any kind.

clue.text: Refined gelatine mixture without a pig's guts

indicators.note: the guts of something are its insides, so the central letter is chosen
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
a mixture stirs its ingredients together, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of the three-letter animal

explanation.surface: A cook boasts a superior jelly made with no pork offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gelatine is often made from pig parts, so the surface is plausible. Remove the I from GELATINE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes graceful, stylish taste or manners, a direct adjective synonym for cultured and polished.

clue.text: Rob and Jason's desire?

blocks.note: first meaning: to swindle or overcharge someone
second meaning: what the Greek hero Jason sailed with the Argonauts to win

explanation.surface: Two men, Rob and Jason, and what one of them wants.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob and Jason look like two friends' names; Rob is a verb and Jason is the hero of Greek myth who sought the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them of money, and the Golden Fleece was the ram's woolly hide that Jason quested after.

clue.text: Receivers cunningly copied store sale

indicators.note: done cunningly means artfully rearranged, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Handlers of stolen goods craftily imitated a shop's sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receivers' suggests people who handle stolen goods, which fits the crooked surface; it really means equipment that receives signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio telescopes are large dishes that pick up radio waves from space, so they are a type of signal-collecting apparatus.

clue.text: Chucked the auditor's chair

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard rather than as spelt

blocks.note: a throne is a royal chair

explanation.surface: Someone tossed the accountant's seat across the room.
explanation.walkthrough: An auditor in the surface is an accountant checking books; here it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Chucked is casual for tossed or hurled, so it matches the past participle of throw exactly.

clue.text: Old bird meets an inexperienced driver outside

blocks.note: ex means former
a tern is a seabird
the indefinite article
L for learner, from the L-plate on a British learner's car

explanation.surface: An elderly woman bumps into a novice motorist out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bird' reads as slang for an elderly woman; split it into its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the exterior surface or beyond something, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Transport lead-free electricity without it getting diverted

indicators.note: free of its lead means stripped of its leading letter
without means lacking, so letters are removed
something diverted is sent along a different route, so the letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A power supply rerouted with no lead pipes, phrased like a utility notice.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first E, then remove one I and one T; the eight letters left rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricycle is a three-wheeled pedal vehicle, so it is one example of a means of getting about.

clue.text: Actors I prevent from leaving reprimand

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
taken as written
to gate a pupil is to confine them to school as punishment

explanation.surface: A director stops the performers walking out and scolds them.
explanation.walkthrough: Gating is a British school punishment: the pupil is kept in and not allowed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to criticise someone severely, so it is a more formal synonym of the verb to scold.

clue.text: Shows the door to vacant juvenile taken in by eccentric sect

indicators.note: something vacant is emptied, so only the outer letters remain
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled
to be taken in is to be held inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cult expels a dim youngster it had recruited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacant' reads as empty-headed, but it means emptied of middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone the door is an idiom for making them leave, the same as throwing them out.

clue.text: Period of instruction is said to be moderate

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is as heard rather than as spelt

blocks.note: a lesson is a session of teaching

explanation.surface: A claim that a class should be kept middling in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderate' looks like an adjective but the definition is the verb: to reduce or tone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to make it less extreme, so the verbs mean reduce or diminish.

clue.text: Chained wild animal eating ants

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run loose

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A savage beast on a chain feeds on insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chained wild' looks like a captive beast, but 'Chained' is the letters and 'wild' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying Australian mammal that feeds largely on termites and other insects.

clue.text: Travelling comedian strangely lacking in energy

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken out
done strangely means in an odd order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A touring stand-up oddly seems to have run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one E out of COMEDIAN and rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes people who wander from place to place without a fixed home, so the adjective fits wandering.

clue.text: Penny amusement for the audience's gratification

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is as heard rather than as spelt

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a British penny
leisure is free time spent on amusement

explanation.surface: A cheap arcade game is laid on to please the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech leisure rhymes with measure, so P plus that sound gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure and gratification are both nouns for the satisfaction or enjoyment felt when a want is met.

clue.text: Essential to slip on choir cloak

indicators.note: something essential to a thing is part of its core, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of slip, on and the start of choir

explanation.surface: Singers must put on a robe before performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' suggests a requirement for singers; here it points inside the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like outer garment with a hole for the head, a kind of sleeveless loose cape.

clue.text: It helps to make sex tremendously intense

indicators.note: a thing that helps make the following words is part of them, so the letters lie within

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of sex and the start of tremendously

explanation.surface: A cheeky tip on how to spice up a love life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like advice from a magazine; the answer is sitting in the middle of two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means of the highest or most severe degree, which is very close to the adjective meaning fierce or strong.

clue.text: Nothing in schedule for early morning caller

indicators.note: one thing put in another sits inside it, so a piece goes within

blocks.note: a roster is a rota or timetable
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A diary has no slot for whoever comes knocking at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early morning caller' suggests a visitor at the door; it is the bird that crows at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, famous for crowing at daybreak, so it is a witty description of a dawn waker.

clue.text: Someone taking charge of Switzerland alongside high-flyer

blocks.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica
an airman flies high, literally

explanation.surface: An ambitious high achiever is put in charge of the Swiss operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flyer' means a high achiever in the surface but literally an aviator in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a meeting or company board, so the role is literally one of being in command.

clue.text: Fear brat's latest mistake

indicators.note: the latest of a sequence comes at the end, so the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of brat
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A parent dreads the next blunder from a spoiled child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fear' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fright, an intensified synonym for the noun meaning dread or alarm.

clue.text: Just perfect!

blocks.note: first meaning: fair, morally correct
second meaning: exactly correct or suitable

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation makes it sound like 'Just perfect!' as praise; the two words are separate meanings of one short adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both moral fairness, as in doing the decent thing, and exact correctness, as in the ideal answer.

clue.text: King briefly affected there with eg ADHD

indicators.note: something affected has been altered by an influence, so the letters are changed around

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch who for a short while had some kind of attention disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' looks like an abbreviation signal but belongs to the definition: this king abdicated in 1936 after less than a year, uncrowned.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward VIII reigned for only eleven months before giving up the British throne to marry Wallis Simpson.

clue.text: Power of a military leader on Cyprus

blocks.note: taken as written
Gen is the abbreviation for general
CY is the international code for Cyprus

explanation.surface: The authority held by a commander stationed on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a charade 'on' can simply mean the next piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency means the capacity to act or exert influence, as in human agency, so it is a noun synonym for capability.

clue.text: Sugary liquid comprising nitrogen and trace elements

indicators.note: the elements of a word are its component letters, here freed to be laid out in another order

blocks.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry label lists what a sweet drink contains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trace elements' reads as one chemistry term; split it so 'elements' acts on the five letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sweet fluid flowers produce to attract bees and other pollinating insects.
